answer: Hardware-backed uniqueness stops Sybil attacks at the root. Each agent must prove it runs in a distinct secure enclave whose key is sealed to one physical chip; the platform checks the maker certificate chain and a fresh quote, so one device yields exactly one identity, marked violet and uncopyable. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand chips, a ridge of real costs rising per identity, while an honest agent pays once. Reusing a chip or bridging the canyon between virtual machines and real hardware fails, since each quote binds to the chip state and a one-time nonce.
